exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 106,225 term pregnancies with non-anomalous singleton fetuses delivered between 37(+0) and 41(+6) weeks.
finding: The incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes (lower birth weights, higher cesarean section rates, increased risks of NRFHRS, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, and emergency cesarean delivery) is higher in the idiopathic oligohydramnios group compared to control pregnancies.
mod_finding: There was a higher incidence of non-reassuring fetal heart rate status in the idiopathic oligohydramnios vaginal delivery group compared to the selective cesarean section group, with the lowest rates of Apgar score <7 at 5 min and cesarean section observed when delivery occurred during 39(+0) to 40(+6) weeks.
